relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (tradesOffAgainst) - two alternative data-migration mechanisms between Couchbase clusters, generally-preferred vs. fallback
relations.evidence: For data migration between Couchbase clusters, [Cross Data Center Replication (XDCR)](xdcr/xdcr.md) is generally recommended. When XDCR cannot be used, the recommended method is to use `cbbackupmgr backup` and `cbbackupmgr restore`.

relations.subject: capella:cbexport-cbimport
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (mustUseInsteadWhen) - cbexport/cbimport should not be used to migrate a Sync Gateway-backed bucket; cbbackupmgr should be used instead
relations.evidence: Using cbexport and cbimport to migrate data from a Couchbase bucket that holds Sync Gateway data can cause the data to be corrupted.

relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresSetting) - cbbackupmgr against a Capella cluster depends on specific disable-option settings tied to what cluster access credentials can read/write
relations.evidence: Use the `--capella` option to disable the backup or restore of data that cannot be read or written by your Capella cluster access credentials.

relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - object generalized to a version concept; the same `--disable-*` flag set is required manually pre-7.6, replaced by a single `--capella` convenience flag at 7.6+
relations.evidence: With Capella clusters running Couchbase Server 7.2, use the following `--disable` options with cbbackupmgr config to configure the backup repository: `--disable-analytics --disable-cluster-analytics --disable-bucket-query --disable-cluster-query`

relations.subject: capella:cluster-access-credentials
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (disablesFeatureFor) - Capella cluster access credentials structurally cannot create buckets, disabling a cbbackupmgr restore convenience option
relations.evidence: Cluster access credentials do not have privileges to create a bucket, so you cannot use the `cbbackupgmr restore` option `--auto-create-buckets` when restoring to a Capella cluster.

relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (gatedByBillingPlan) - cbbackupmgr is presented as the ONLY backup/migration path available to free tier operational clusters, since UI backup options are unavailable to them (see manage-backup.json)
relations.evidence: This example uses `cbbackupmgr` CLI to migrate data from a free tier operational cluster to a paid operational cluster.

relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - a self-managed Community Edition source cluster requires the cbbackupmgr CLI specifically (not an alternative tool) to restore into a Capella provisioned cluster
relations.evidence: A self-managed cluster can be either an Enterprise or Community Edition cluster. If you're using the Community Edition of Couchbase Server, you need to use the `cbbackupmgr` CLI from the command line tools package to restore to the Capella provisioned cluster.

notable_absence.finding: No capella-role:* gate appears anywhere on this CLI-tool page - access control here is entirely a function of the cluster access credential's own read/write scope (data-plane), not a Capella management-plane role. This is a genuine structural difference from the UI-based backup/restore pages in this same batch (manage-backup.md, manage-restore.md), which gate on Project Owner/Organization Owner instead.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest evidence in the batch that Capella has TWO independent backup/restore access-control mechanisms depending on the path used: the Capella UI path is gated by capella-role:* (management-plane authorization), while the cbbackupmgr CLI path is gated by data-plane cluster access credential scope (what the credential itself can read/write) - the two never overlap or substitute for each other on this page.
cross_product_finding: Recurrence of the known Enterprise/Community edition-badge anomaly, but in a notably different shape than prior rounds: here the edition distinction describes a SELF-MANAGED source cluster being migrated INTO Capella, not Capella itself (which has no Enterprise/Community distinction) - so this is not actually an anomaly on a Capella page in the same sense as prior findings, it's a legitimate cross-product edition reference because the self-managed cluster genuinely has editions. Flagging the distinction for the reconciler rather than conflating it with the other-round Capella-page-badge anomaly.
